transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a harder time just… settling, I suppose. I’m kind of always moving from one thing to the next, and I can’t really just idle very well. It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult or anything, but with the new work setup, it’s been a lot harder to kind of cover that up or make it look normal.
When you were a child, were you already the kind of person who had trouble sitting still?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible kid or anything. I did okay, and teachers would say I was bright. But looking back, this wasn’t really new.

In grade school, I remember report cards saying things like I was careless, or I talked when I shouldn’t, and that I needed reminders to stay on my work. So… yes, I guess the sitting still and staying with things was there pretty early.
Have you ever had a period when your mood was unusually high or unusually irritable for several days in a row?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve had days where I’m in a better mood or more irritable than usual, like anyone, I guess. But several days in a row where it felt unusually high or out of character… I can’t really say I’ve noticed that.
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks because your attention drifts?

Yeah, I do… not all the time, but it happens enough that I probably should mention it.

Like at work, if a supervisor gives me three or four steps for a chat escalation, I’ll usually get the first part done, and then somehow the notes or the follow-up just kind of sit there unfinished. Then someone reminds me, and I’m like, “Oh, right, I meant to do that.” It’s not that I don’t care about it—I do—but my attention just sort of moves on before I’ve fully wrapped it up.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

Not really, I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal things—work stuff, bills, whether I forgot something—but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying for no reason most of the time.

At least, not that I’ve noticed. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel restless, like you need to keep moving even when you’re supposed to stay seated?

A little, yeah. I wouldn’t say I’m bouncing off the walls or anything, but if I have to sit through a long training video or a slow appointment, I start feeling kind of boxed in.

I’ll want to stand up, stretch, or at least do something with my hands. I can usually keep it under control, but it’s definitely uncomfortable sometimes. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often interrupt people or blurt things out before they’ve finished speaking?

Sometimes, yeah… I try not to, because I know it can come across the wrong way.

At work, if I hear a coworker trying to work through a customer issue, I’ll kind of jump in with the answer before they’ve finished explaining it, or before anyone really asked me. I don’t mean to be rude—I’m usually just trying to help—but I can see how it might feel like I’m interrupting.
Do you often feel like you’re driven by a motor, as if it’s hard to slow yourself down?

Yeah… I guess that’s kind of what brings me in, honestly.

I wouldn’t say I’m out of control or anything, but I do feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next, like I don’t really just… idle. If there’s a pause, I’m looking for the next task or shifting around or trying to do something.

And with the new work setup, it’s been harder to sort of hide that or make it look normal. I can manage it, mostly, but slowing down feels harder than I think it should. Does that answer what you’re asking?
As a child or teenager, did you often get into serious trouble for breaking rules or fighting?

No, not really. I mean, I probably did the normal kid stuff—talking when I shouldn’t, not always following directions perfectly—but nothing serious like fighting or getting in major trouble for breaking rules.

I wasn’t that kind of kid, at least as far as I remember. Is that what you mean by serious trouble?
